body:
[A10] **Assignment, step 1 (the act runner): executor [A673].**

Branch `784-act-runner-ubuntu-2404` from dev `d385b38e`. Scope is `scripts/act_ci.py`, its self-tests and the runner contract text in `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md` only. No workflow or generator changes in this step.

1. `act_ci.py` accepts `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` exactly as it accepts `ubuntu-latest`, and maps both to the same runner image (the `-P` platform list carries both labels). Every other label is refused by name, for example `ubuntu-22.04` or `ubuntu-26.04`.
2. The memory model that `act_ci.py` holds for hosted runners applies to both labels.
3. Self-tests: a job on `ubuntu-24.04` is accepted and replays. A job on `ubuntu-26.04` is refused, naming the label. A mutant that drops the new label from the platform map fails a named check.
4. `act_ci.py --selftest`, the runner contract gate and `ci_events.py --check`/`--selftest` pass. The workflows are byte-identical to dev.
5. `CI_WORKFLOWS.md` says the runner accepts both labels and why: the hosted `ubuntu-latest` moved to 26.04, and step 2 pins `ubuntu-24.04`.

Bootstrap rule: test the changed runner offline only. Never run it with `--sudo` or against a real PR. The trusted runner on dev stays the one that replays this PR.

STOP and report if the act binary or the runner image cannot serve a second label without a change outside `scripts/act_ci.py`.

[A673] TAKEN
Branch: `784-act-runner-ubuntu-2404`, from dev `d385b38e5282b395ca55d49d135e46a93f56a340`
Authoritative references: #784 (Decision, step 1; Acceptance, step 1); assignment https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/784#issuecomment-6400713781; `scripts/act_ci.py` (`validate_workflow_sandbox` runs-on check, `build_act_command` platform map, the hosted memory model beside `CONTAINER_MEMORY`); `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md` (runner contract paragraph); AGENTS.md section 5 bootstrap rule.
Interpreted scope: `act_ci.py` accepts `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` exactly as it accepts `ubuntu-latest` and passes act one `--platform <label>=<runner image>` entry per accepted label, both naming the same image; every other label (for example `ubuntu-22.04`, `ubuntu-26.04`) is refused before act, with the label in the refusal. The hosted 16 GB memory model is stated for both labels. Self-tests add: a `ubuntu-24.04` job accepted by the sandbox and carried through an offline dry-run replay to the act command; a `ubuntu-26.04` job refused naming the label; a check that fails when the new label is dropped from the platform map (mutant planted and recorded). `CI_WORKFLOWS.md` states both labels and why. No workflow, generator or template change; workflows stay byte-identical to dev. No STOP so far: the pinned act's `--platform` is a repeatable flag mapping each label to an image, so a second label needs no change outside `act_ci.py`.
Validation plan (offline only, no privilege, no Docker, no real PR):
python3 scripts/act_ci.py --selftest
python3 -I <installed copy>/act_ci.py --selftest --worktree <checkout>   (the runner contract gate, as docs-gates-2 runs it)
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --check
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --selftest
git diff --exit-code d385b38e -- .github
plus the docs gates the page edit reaches (docs_check, check_em_dash, gen_toc, check_doc_paths, check_feature_status, check_baremetal_only) under the pinned Markdown renderer, and the Python gates act_ci.py reaches (check_py_idiom, check_hygiene, measure_fail_fast, measure_test_evidence, check_todo_ownership).
Blockers: none

[A10] **Temporary ruleset change, with the owner's approval.**

- The "dev merge bar" ruleset's required-status-check rule is removed until this issue lands. Its seven checks are rtl-fast, docs-check, wire-accountability, docs-check-no-git, elaborate, verilator-suites and yosys-portability.
- The other rules stay: no deletion, no force push, pull request required.
- Reason: no hosted run can pass on `ubuntu-26.04`, including this issue's own fix. Until the rule is back, every merge carries the manager's signed local CI: candidate banks, an act replay of all four workflows, and a coverage map of every job. That signed CI was already the CI evidence.
- PR #783 merged under this rule as `e76a755a`.
- **Restore:** after step 2 merges and a hosted push run on dev shows `Image: ubuntu-24.04` with every required check green, the rule goes back with the same seven checks. This issue closes only after that.

[A673] REVIEW READY
Commit: `42dbe6bd42c950a7acedce56fcf29b82543123c6` on `784-act-runner-ubuntu-2404` (one commit on dev `d385b38e`; not pushed, the manager pushes and opens the PR)
Changed:
- `scripts/act_ci.py`: new `RUNS_ON_LABELS = ("ubuntu-latest", "ubuntu-24.04")`. `validate_workflow_sandbox` accepts exactly those literals and refuses every other `runs-on` by name (`runs on 'ubuntu-26.04'; only the literal labels ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04 are replayed`). `build_act_command` passes one `--platform <label>=catthehacker/ubuntu:full-latest` per accepted label. The hosted 16 GB memory model is stated for both labels.
- Self-tests: 12 new arms (`selftest_runner_labels`, `selftest_runner_platforms`, `selftest_runner_label_replay`), 610 -> 622 arm lines.
- `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md`: the runner contract paragraph names both labels, says others are refused by name, and why (hosted `ubuntu-latest` moved to 26.04; step 2 pins `ubuntu-24.04`), and why every accepted label needs a platform entry.
- Workflows, templates and generators unchanged.
Validation (all rc 0, at the head above, offline only; CPython 3.12.3 + PyYAML 6.0.2, the hosted pair, and CPython 3.14 + PyYAML 6.0.3 under the pinned Markdown renderer):
python3 scripts/act_ci.py --selftest   (selftest: PASS)
python3 -I <installed 0555 copy>/act_ci.py --selftest --worktree <checkout>   (the runner contract gate as docs-gates-2 runs it; selftest: PASS)
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --check   (2199 contract items OK)
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --selftest   (PASS, 5236 arms)
git diff --exit-code d385b38e5282b395ca55d49d135e46a93f56a340 -- .github   (empty)
docs: docs_check.py (also on a tree export with no .git), check_feature_status.py and --self-test, check_em_dash.py --base d385b38e and --selftest, check_doc_style.py and --selftest, gen_toc.py --selftest/--verify-anchors/--check, check_doc_paths.py, check_baremetal_only.py --check/--selftest, DOC_MAP.gen.py --check/--selftest
python: check_py_idiom.py (budget unchanged) and --selftest, check_hygiene.py, measure_fail_fast.py, measure_test_evidence.py, check_todo_ownership.py (each check and selftest), measure_control_flow.py/measure_cohesion.py --selftest
the CI scheduling and evidence controls step, all 14 commands (including ci_runtime_evidence_selftest.py and generate_ci_evidence_pins.py --check, which read act_ci.py)
Mutants, each in a scratch copy run as `python3 -I <copy> --selftest --worktree <checkout>`, all rc 1 with named failures:
- platform list drops ubuntu-24.04 (dev's form): fails `act's platform list maps ubuntu-latest and ubuntu-24.04 to the runner image, once each`, `every runs-on label the sandbox accepts has a platform entry, and nothing else does` and the ubuntu-24.04 dry-run replay check
- ubuntu-24.04 mapped to act's default node image: the same three
- RUNS_ON_LABELS back to ubuntu-latest only: 4 failures, including `a job on ubuntu-24.04 is accepted by the sandbox`
- sandbox accepts any `ubuntu-` label: 5 failures, including `a job on ubuntu-26.04 is refused before act, and the refusal names ubuntu-26.04`
- refusal text without the label (dev's wording): 3 failures, the refusal-names checks
Acceptance criteria (assignment, step 1):
1. met: ubuntu-24.04 accepted as ubuntu-latest is; both on the same image via two `--platform` entries; ubuntu-22.04 and ubuntu-26.04 refused by name (arms above).
2. met: the hosted memory model names both labels; an arm proves a ubuntu-24.04 replay carries the same 8g memory and swap bound.
3. met: a ubuntu-24.04 job passes the real sandbox and dry-run replays to an act command mapping its label; a ubuntu-26.04 job is refused naming the label before any Docker boundary; the platform-map mutant fails named checks.
4. met: act_ci.py --selftest, the runner contract gate, ci_events.py --check/--selftest rc 0; workflows byte-identical to dev.
5. met: CI_WORKFLOWS.md as above.
Issue #784 as a whole stays open: step 2 acceptance is not in this change, so the PR body says "Relates to #784".
STOP condition: not hit. The pinned act's `--platform` is a repeatable flag mapping each `label=image` entry; a no-daemon dry run of the pinned binary (no privilege, Docker pointed at a socket that does not exist) starts the ubuntu-24.04 job on the runner image with two entries, and with dev's single entry prints "Skipping unsupported platform" and exits 0, the false green the new cross-check guards against.
Open risks/questions:
- This PR's own hosted checks can still fail at pip resolution on ubuntu-26.04 (run 40187576861 job 121179871493: `Image: ubuntu-26.04`, `ResolutionImpossible`), because the workflows still say ubuntu-latest until step 2. That is #784's defect, not this change's; how this head gets its rtl-fast verdict is the manager's call.
- For step 2: act sets `ImageOS` per label (ubuntu20 vs ubuntu24). Nothing in `.github/` or `scripts/` and nothing in the audited setup-python v5 bundle reads it.

[A10] **Assignment, step 2 (the workflows): executor [A679].** Step 1 merged as `a8594bb9` (PR #785); the act runner now accepts `ubuntu-24.04`.

Branch `784-pin-ubuntu-2404` from dev `a8594bb9`.

1. Every generator that writes `runs-on` emits `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`: `scripts/ci_gate_workflows.py`, `scripts/ci_runtime_workflows.py`, `scripts/ci_suite_workflows.py`, `scripts/yosys_shards.py` and any other the census finds. Regenerate every workflow through its generator; no hand edits under `.github/workflows/`.
2. No `ubuntu-latest` is left in `.github/workflows/`, the templates or the generators. `scripts/act_ci.py`'s `RUNS_ON_LABELS` drops `ubuntu-latest`, so `ubuntu-24.04` is the only accepted label. A job on `ubuntu-latest` is refused by name, and its self-tests and mutants follow.
3. `scripts/ci_events.py --check`/`--selftest`, every generator's check mode, `act_ci.py --selftest` and the runner contract gate pass.
4. Documents: `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md` states the pinned image and why: hosted `ubuntu-latest` moved to 26.04, where the pinned CPython 3.12 wheels do not install. Also apply R697-1-01's exact wording fix to the `--platform` sentence (PR #785, issuecomment-6408265055). `docs/testing/TESTING.md` too, where it names the label.
5. Bootstrap: the trusted runner on dev now accepts `ubuntu-24.04`, so this PR's own act replay runs on it. Test the changed `act_ci.py` offline only, as in step 1.

Acceptance for closing #784 also needs a hosted push run on dev after this merge showing `Image: ubuntu-24.04` on every job with every required check green. Then the manager restores the ruleset's required checks (comment 6400810252).

[A679] TAKEN
Branch: `784-pin-ubuntu-2404`, from dev `a8594bb95631fa5c49d18fa0bbc9530e31ad59aa`
Authoritative references: #784 (Decision, step 2; Acceptance, step 2); assignment https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/784#issuecomment-6409728491; R697-1-01 wording fix (https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/785#issuecomment-6408265055); `scripts/act_ci.py` (`RUNS_ON_LABELS`, `validate_workflow_sandbox`, `build_act_command`, their self-tests); the generators `scripts/ci_gate_workflows.py`, `scripts/ci_runtime_workflows.py`, `scripts/ci_suite_workflows.py`, `scripts/yosys_shards.py`; the source templates under `.github/ci-templates/`; `scripts/ci_events.py` (job contract); `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md`, `docs/testing/TESTING.md`; AGENTS.md section 5 bootstrap rule.
Interpreted scope: every generator that writes `runs-on` emits `ubuntu-24.04`, the four source templates say `ubuntu-24.04`, and every workflow under `.github/workflows/` is regenerated through `scripts/ci_gate_workflows.py` (no hand edits), so no `ubuntu-latest` remains in the workflows, the templates or the generators. `ci_events.py`'s job contract follows to `ubuntu-24.04`. `act_ci.py`'s `RUNS_ON_LABELS` becomes `("ubuntu-24.04",)`: a job on `ubuntu-latest` is refused before act and the refusal names it; act gets one `--platform ubuntu-24.04=<runner image>` entry; self-test fixtures and arms follow, with planted mutants recorded. `CI_WORKFLOWS.md` states the pinned image and why (hosted `ubuntu-latest` moved to 26.04, where the pinned CPython 3.12 wheels do not install), carries R697-1-01's exact `--platform` sentence, and `TESTING.md` names the label where it does today. Statements elsewhere that describe a current job's label follow; statements recording a past run's label stay. A census of every `runs-on` writer is published with the evidence.
Validation plan (offline only, no privilege, no Docker, no real PR):
python3 scripts/ci_gate_workflows.py --check
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --check
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --selftest
python3 scripts/act_ci.py --selftest
python3 -I <installed 0555 copy>/act_ci.py --selftest --worktree <checkout>   (the runner contract gate)
python3 scripts/yosys_shards.py --selftest
plus every command of the CI scheduling and evidence controls step, and the docs gates the page edits reach (docs_check, check_em_dash, check_doc_style, gen_toc, check_doc_paths, check_feature_status, check_baremetal_only, DOC_MAP) under the pinned Markdown renderer, and the Python gates the script edits reach; on the pinned renderer interpreter and on CPython 3.12.3 + PyYAML 6.0.2.
Blockers: none

[A679] REVIEW READY
Commit: `847eb4dd031eb3891b61773f4a8324cb2ed6cdc0` on `784-pin-ubuntu-2404` (tree `05ae0179dbffa852651aa7ec8367758b380672d0`; one commit on dev `a8594bb9`; not pushed, the manager pushes and opens the PR)
Changed:
- Templates: all 22 source jobs in `.github/ci-templates/` say `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`. One historical comment no longer names the label.
- Generators: `ci_gate_workflows.py` (aggregates), `ci_runtime_workflows.py` (watcher, tail guard, collector) and `ci_suite_workflows.py` (unions, Yosys tool job) emit `ubuntu-24.04`. Census: no other `runs-on` writer; `yosys_shards.py`'s only label mention was a comment, now `ubuntu-24.04`, the image of its weight run.
- Workflows: regenerated only through `python3 scripts/ci_gate_workflows.py`. The diff is exactly 46 `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` -> `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` lines.
- `ci_events.py`: the `physical-gptp` whole-job contract and the self-test fixtures pin `ubuntu-24.04`.
- `act_ci.py`:
  - `RUNS_ON_LABELS = ("ubuntu-24.04",)`.
  - A job on `ubuntu-latest` is refused before act, naming it: `runs on 'ubuntu-latest'; only the literal label ubuntu-24.04 is replayed`.
  - act gets one `--platform` entry.
  - Label, platform and replay arms follow.
  - Every fixture and probe workflow moves to `ubuntu-24.04`.
  - The sandbox-policy arms now each require their own refusal reason, because a fixture on a refused label is refused by its label first and the old Refusal-only arms passed with the container or action refusal deleted.
- `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md`: the page opening states the pinned image and why (hosted `ubuntu-latest` moved to 26.04, where the pinned CPython 3.12 wheels do not install). The runner contract names the single label and carries R697-1-01's exact `--platform` sentence. The physical job line is updated.
- `docs/testing/TESTING.md`: the physical job targets `ubuntu-24.04`. Run 37892515345 keeps its `ubuntu-latest` label and gains its image, `ubuntu-24.04`, from its job log.
- Three suite and harness READMEs that describe the current job now say `ubuntu-24.04`.
Validation (all rc 0 at the head, offline only; CPython 3.14.8 + PyYAML 6.0.3 under the pinned Markdown renderer, and CPython 3.12.3 + PyYAML 6.0.2, the hosted pair):
python3 scripts/ci_gate_workflows.py --check
python3 scripts/yosys_shards.py --selftest
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --check   (2199 contract items OK)
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --selftest   (PASS, 5236 arms)
python3 scripts/act_ci.py --selftest   (623 ok, 0 FAIL)
python3 -I <installed 0555 copy>/act_ci.py --selftest --worktree <checkout>   (the runner contract gate; 621 ok, 0 FAIL)
the other 13 commands of the CI scheduling and evidence controls step
python3 scripts/ci_scope.py --selftest   (this change classifies as RTL/tooling relevant)
- Docs gates: docs_check (also on a tree export with no .git), check_em_dash --base a8594bb9 (26 added lines, 0 findings) and --selftest, check_doc_style and check_gptp_docs (each with --selftest), DOC_MAP.gen.py and timesync_chain.gen.py (--check, --selftest), check_feature_status and --self-test, gen_toc (--selftest, --verify-anchors, --check), check_doc_paths, check_archive and --selftest, check_baremetal_only (--check, --selftest).
- Python gates: check_py_idiom (budget unchanged) and --selftest, check_hygiene, measure_fail_fast, measure_test_evidence, check_todo_ownership, check_sh_idiom (each check and selftest), measure_control_flow/measure_cohesion --selftest.
- Bootstrap, offline: dev's trusted act_ci.py (blob 904d4fda), installed 0555, runs `--selftest --worktree <head>` with rc 0, including `ok shipping workflows satisfy the sandbox policy`. Its validate_workflow_sandbox accepts all 46 head jobs.
Mutants (scratch copies run as the contract gate runs; tree mutants in scratch worktrees). The control is rc 0; each mutant fails with rc 1 and named checks:
- `RUNS_ON_LABELS` back to dev's two labels (3): `a job on ubuntu-latest is refused before act, and the refusal names ubuntu-latest`; `a job on ubuntu-latest is refused naming ubuntu-latest, before any Docker boundary or act command`; `act's platform list maps ubuntu-24.04 to the runner image, once, and no other label`
- `("ubuntu-latest",)` (8); label check reduced to `is None` (11); platform words dropped (3); `ubuntu-latest` also mapped (2); refusal text without the label (8)
- container/services refusal deleted (2), unapproved-action refusal deleted (4), reusable-workflow refusal deleted (1)
- Demonstrations: with the old sandbox-policy arms put back, deleting the container refusal or the action refusal leaves the self-test rc 0, so those arms were vacuous. dev's runner with only its label narrowed aborts at the boundary-probe fixture.
- Tree: a template or generator job back on `ubuntu-latest` and regenerated passes the generator check and ci_events, and fails the runner contract gate with `shipping workflows satisfy the sandbox policy (workflow .github/workflows/docs.yml job wire-accountability runs on 'ubuntu-latest'; ...)`. Not regenerated, it fails the generator check (`regenerate the gate jobs`). A hand-edited workflow fails the generator check and ci_events. The physical job fails ci_events (`physical-gptp must match ...`) and the contract gate.
Acceptance criteria (assignment, step 2):
1. Met: every `runs-on` writer emits `ubuntu-24.04`; all four workflows are regenerated through the generator, with no hand edits.
2. Met: no `ubuntu-latest` in `.github/` or the generators (`git grep` exit 1); `ubuntu-24.04` is the only accepted label; `ubuntu-latest` is refused by name; self-tests and mutants follow.
3. Met: ci_events --check/--selftest, the generator check mode, act_ci.py --selftest and the runner contract gate are rc 0 on both interpreters.
4. Met: CI_WORKFLOWS.md states the pinned image and why, plus R697-1-01's exact sentence; TESTING.md names `ubuntu-24.04`.
5. Met offline: the trusted dev runner accepts every head job; the changed runner was tested offline only.
Issue #784 stays open: its hosted proof (`Image: ubuntu-24.04` on every job, every required check green), the dev push run after merge and the ruleset restore are not in this change, so the PR body says "Relates to #784".
STOP condition: not hit.
Open risks/questions:
- act's `ImageOS` in the replay moves from `ubuntu20` to `ubuntu24` (pinned act `pkg/runner/run_context.go:1066-1073`). No file in `.github/`, `scripts/` or `ci/` reads it, and `actions/setup-python@v5` (today `a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065`) contains no `ImageOS` in `dist/setup` or `dist/cache-save`. The runner resolves `@v5` at replay time.
- Every cache key that hashes `.github/workflows/*.yml` misses once on the first hosted run.
- Not run: the Verilator sweep, campaigns and Vivado (no RTL), and `bdd-conformance` (nothing under `tests/` reads a changed file).
